title: Handle eggs for setting at a hatchery

lessons.title: Receiving and selecting hatching eggs
lessons.html:
Receiving and selecting hatching eggs

Hatching eggs come from breeder (parent stock) farms. Each egg holds a living embryo that can become a chick. Rough handling, heat, cold or dirt can kill the embryo before the egg is ever set. Your care decides how many chicks hatch.

Receiving eggs

  1. Check the delivery note: farm, flock number, lay date and number of trays.
  2. Look at the truck. It should be clean and cool, with eggs protected from sun and rain.
  3. Off-load trays or trolleys gently. Do not bump or drop them.
  4. Move eggs quickly into the egg store.
  5. Record the delivery in the hatchery book or system.

Selecting eggs for setting

Only good eggs should go into the setter. Remove eggs that are:

  • cracked or have thin, rough or soft shells;
  • very dirty or soiled with droppings;
  • very small, very large or badly shaped;
  • double-yolked (very large) where the hatchery rule says so.

Put rejected eggs in the reject trays and record the number. A high number of rejects from one farm should be reported to your supervisor, because it points to a problem on that farm.

Hygiene

  • Wash and sanitise your hands before handling eggs.
  • Wear clean hatchery clothing.
  • Never wash hatching eggs with water unless the hatchery has a set method. Wet shells let germs into the egg.
  • Eggs may be fumigated or sanitised by trained staff only, following the hatchery procedure.

Turning trays the right way

Hatching eggs are set with the blunt end (air cell end) up and the pointed end down. Eggs set upside down hatch poorly.

lessons.title: Storing and setting eggs
lessons.html:
Storing and setting eggs

The egg store

Hatching eggs are kept in a cool egg store until they are set. Heat starts the embryo growing too early and it then dies. Very cold eggs can also be damaged.

  • Keep the egg store at the temperature and humidity the hatchery manager sets.
  • Check and record the store temperature and humidity at set times each day.
  • Keep the doors closed. Do not leave trolleys of eggs in the sun or in a hot passage.
  • Report at once if the cooling unit fails.

Storage time

Hatchability drops the longer eggs are stored. Use eggs in order of lay date, oldest first, unless the manager gives a different setting plan. Label each trolley with farm, flock and lay date so the eggs can be traced.

Preparing to set

  1. Check the setting plan: which eggs, how many, which setter.
  2. Eggs that come out of a cool store are often warmed slowly to room temperature before setting. This stops water forming on the shell (sweating), which lets germs in. Follow the hatchery's pre-warming procedure.
  3. Load the setter trays carefully, blunt end up.
  4. Fill the setter in the order the procedure says and record the setter number and position of each flock.

Lifting and safety

Egg trolleys are heavy. Push them, do not pull, and keep hands clear of the setter doors and racks. Ask for help on ramps.

Records

Good records let the hatchery trace any hatch problem back to the farm and flock. Record egg numbers, rejects, store temperatures and setting details every time.

Key points

  • Handle hatching eggs gently; the embryo inside is alive.
  • Reject cracked, dirty and misshaped eggs and record them.
  • Keep the egg store at the set temperature and check it daily.
  • Set eggs blunt end up and oldest lay date first.
  • Label and record every batch so it can be traced.
